title: Harness Capability Profile (v1)
description: What the harness that will replay these plans can actually do. frameladder plans against its own interpreter, where every variable is settable and every operation replayable; a real harness is narrower and projects a plan down to what it supports, dropping the rest. A plan that depended on a dropped value still runs and simply means nothing. This document turns that projection into a constraint the planner can honour before it spends any budget. Sections may be omitted; an absent section states no constraint rather than an empty one.

program.description: Program the profile describes, for the harness's own bookkeeping.

injectable_variables.description: Entry-state variables the harness can set. A binding on anything else makes a plan unrepresentable. Omit the section entirely to state no constraint; an empty array means the harness can inject nothing.

replayable_operations.description: External operations the harness can mock, keyed the way frameladder keys them: READ:FILE, OPEN-INPUT:FILE, CALL:PGM, EXEC:SQL:SELECT, EXEC:CICS:READ. Mode is part of the identity because it decides the outcome.

fields.description: Payload fields this operation can set. Omit for no restriction.

max_outcomes.description: Longest outcome series the harness can replay for this operation. 0 or absent means no stated limit. A read loop needs a series, not a value.

uncovered_directions.description: The work list. Targeting these rather than deep paragraphs is what stops a plan succeeding on code that was already covered. `ordinal` is the decision's position within its paragraph -- a line does not identify a decision, because COPY expansion puts many on one line.

attempts.description: What happened when the harness ran earlier plans, against the real compiled program. `first_missing_frame` is the valuable field: the run demonstrably reproduces the frame before it, so that frame is a far better place to plan from than the entry paragraph.
